prompt:
REPAINT the room from IMAGE 2 according to this locked art direction. IMAGE 1, the Girls' Frontline 2 room, is our main reference for sophisticated neutral colour relations, painted game-background edges and believable inhabited atmosphere. Do not copy its room or props. IMAGE 2 is only our existing CAMERA/SPACE plan: retain the huge close LEFT foreground chair and projecting diagonal armrest, wide left-middle work desk, compatible working chair, rear utility storage and right-wall sleeping berth/fireplace. Preserve human scale, desk width, knee clearance and central walk route. Keep this layout and camera, but visibly REDRAW the painting, colour and material treatment; do not merely add a colour filter or more objects.

The setting remains an inhabited postmodern expedition camp outside a winter city about 100 years in the future, with refined civilian modular furniture, a few broad matte insulated panels, practical softened/chamfered corners and minimal fittings. Room dry; winter only outside and at the small modern fireplace.

1. REBUILD COLOUR RELATIONS. The old image is too uniformly dark grey-brown. Give walls a readable soft stone GREY-GREEN midtone, rear cabinetry a distinct desaturated GREY-TEAL, worktop and bedding a neutral WARM IVORY/off-white, fabric a GRAPHITE BLUE-GREY, shadows a quiet BLUE-GREY, and the blanket a tiny muted TERRACOTTA accent. These material colour families must be visibly distinguishable even at small size, harmonious and comfortably neutral like reference 1. Do not make everything brown, yellow, green or blue. Lift selected interior middle values with pale neutral diffuse window bounce, while retaining clear hierarchy: exterior window brightest; near chair darkest but readable; desk/map and pillow/bed linen catch the light; rear cabinet and floor recede. One consistent soft overcast window light unifies everything. Warm-white task light and amber fireplace remain SMALL local sources. No golden shafts, global yellow tint, crushed blacks or uniformly brighter room.

2. REPAINT MATERIAL AND EDGES. Simplify the large near chair upholstery into 2-3 broad painted value planes, with soft fabric form and a few meaningful seams; REMOVE all dense woven speckle and repetitive fabric grain. Replace the camouflage jacket with a PLAIN solid slate-blue garment, loose large folds, no pattern or arm patch. The foreground silhouette/armrest maintains strong perspective, not photographic depth-of-field blur. Work-group edges are selectively crisp. Rear-wall outlines, panel seams and dark cabinet boundaries partly disappear into adjacent colours/shadow. Use subtly layered hand-painted colour planes and a few soft brush transitions in broad surfaces, not uniformly smooth vector fill or continuous dark outlines. Matte metal gets only a few narrow local edge highlights where light actually hits it; REMOVE continuous glowing rims and model-render polish. Floor is a subdued matte NEUTRAL grey painted plane with a few broad perspective joins and diffuse contact shadows; REMOVE every reflection, glossy sheen, mottled texture and scratch pattern. Our goal is the selective painted finish of reference 1, without photo/3D material detail overpowering the picture.

3. HUMAN USE WITHOUT EXTRA CLUTTER. Turn the working chair slightly, about 15 degrees, and pull it out a little as if someone just stood up, maintaining the aisle. Desk shows one unfolded map, an open document folio, one compact communication terminal, one useful task lamp and ONE mug within a seated worker's reach; preserve substantial usable tabletop. REMOVE the small equipment cases on the desk and the independent case under the chair. Keep any built-in drawer at the far-left table end quiet. The rear lower cabinet has exactly TWO identical slate-grey equipment cases with the same dimensions, colour and latches. Replace the large transparent water-bottle dispenser with ONE compact integrated clean-water/tea unit; thermos and cup stay together on one small tray, no row of scattered vessels. Bedding/pillow slightly offset with just a few loose large folds; blanket hem does not hang towards fire. Retain the small enclosed rectangular fireplace at front-right, properly separated from bedding by clear floor and a fireproof partition. No decorative props, extra boxes, plant, poster, labels, symbols, signs, equipment clutter or random gadgets.

4. OUTSIDE STAYS QUIET. Snow and a VERY faint distant modern city indicated by a few low-contrast pale blue-grey architectural masses, almost no detail. No mountains, trees, rocks, roads, sharp city windows or photographic gaussian bokeh. Foreground large dark chair frames the working area; middle desk is most readable; far storage and exterior lose detail naturally. Full 16:9 commercial anime game background, convincingly painted depth and realistic functional perspective, calm comfortable lived-in atmosphere. No people, UI, text, logos, neon, antique/rustic objects or indoor snow.
